skill.name: research
skill.description: Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a Markdown file in the repo. Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading legwork delegated to a background agent.
skill.summary: Research primary sources and save cited findings as a Markdown report.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: No static security findings were present. Manual review of SKILL.md found a prompt-only research workflow with no prompt injection, credential handling, executable code, or data exfiltration intent.

content.user_title: Research Primary Sources With Cited Notes
content.value_statement: Reliable technical research takes time and source checking. This skill investigates primary sources and records cited findings in a Markdown file.
actual_capabilities: Investigates user questions against official docs, source code, specs, and first-party APIs.
Follows claims back to the source that owns them.
Delegates reading work to a background agent when available.
Writes findings into one Markdown file.
Cites sources for each claim in the research note.
Saves the note using the repository notes convention when one exists.
limitations: It depends on available access to primary sources.
It does not define a rigid report template beyond a single cited Markdown file.
It may need user direction when the repository has no notes convention.
It is not a substitute for legal, medical, security, or compliance review.

use_cases.title: API Behavior Verification
use_cases.description: Confirm how an API works before changing code.

use_cases.title: Documentation Research
use_cases.description: Collect official citations for docs, guides, or release notes.

use_cases.title: Product Discovery
use_cases.description: Research platform capabilities before scoping a feature.

prompt_templates.title: Research a Single Question
prompt_templates.prompt: Research whether React Server Components can access browser APIs. Use primary sources and save a cited Markdown note.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Official Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the official caching options in Next.js. Cite primary docs for each claim and write one Markdown report.

prompt_templates.title: Trace an API Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate when an API added background processing support. Use official docs or changelogs and cite every dated claim.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Decision Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Research the risks of migrating our package manager to pnpm. Use primary sources, separate facts from recommendations, and save the brief in the repo notes.

output_examples.input: Research how the TypeScript compiler resolves path aliases.
output_examples.output: The skill creates a Markdown note with official TypeScript references, a concise behavior summary, and cited claims.

output_examples.input: Find primary sources for OAuth 2.1 changes relevant to our app.
output_examples.output: The skill records relevant specification sections, highlights implementation impact, and cites each claim.

output_examples.input: Investigate whether a library supports a specific deployment target.
output_examples.output: The skill checks official docs or source code, states supported targets, and saves the evidence in a repository note.

best_practices: Ask one clear research question and name the decision it should support.
Tell the agent where research notes usually live in the repository.
Request primary sources and citations for claims that affect product or engineering decisions.
anti_patterns: Using the skill for unsourced opinions or general brainstorming.
Asking it to summarize secondary articles without tracing claims to primary sources.
Treating the research note as final legal, medical, or compliance advice.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces a single Markdown file with findings and source citations.

faq.question: Can it browse the web?
faq.answer: It can use whatever browsing or file-reading tools the host agent provides.

faq.question: Does it write code?
faq.answer: No. The skill is designed to research and write notes, not modify application code.

faq.question: Where are notes saved?
faq.answer: It follows existing repository conventions. If none exist, it chooses a sensible location and reports it.

faq.question: What sources does it prefer?
faq.answer: It prefers official docs, source code, specifications, and first-party APIs.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it when you need source-backed answers before making a documentation, product, or engineering decision.
